subject: Discovery recap & integration/onboarding plan - FastRetail PoC
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena@fastretail.co>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Mar 2026 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap & integration/onboarding plan - FastRetail PoC

Hi Elena / Tom —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we’re all aligned and have clear next steps for the PoC: 

Pain points you shared:
- Generating personalized product descriptions at scale is adding ~2–3s latency to page load in your existing pipeline.
- Current embedding-based search struggles with seasonal synonyms and product attributes, driving search quality regressions.
- Cost unpredictability when traffic spikes; you’re looking to reduce per-token cost while keeping latency SLOs.

Current stack & constraints:
- Backend: Node.js microservices, Python analytics batch jobs.
- Serving today: in-house embedding service + Redis cache; models currently hosted via a managed endpoint (vendor X).
- Security: must stay within FastRetail VPC for SKU-sensitive requests during PoC; SOC 2 evidence required for production.

Success criteria for PoC (agreed):
1) Reduce 95th percentile token latency for generation API from 2.8s -> <=1.2s for standard product-descriptions workload.
2) Improve embedding search recall on seasonal queries by +6–8% (measured via your eval set).
3) Demonstrate predictable unit cost at target traffic (simulate 5k qps for 2-hour window).

Proposed PoC / integration plan (timeline & owners):
- Week 0 (this week): Kickoff, sign PoC MSA. (Owner: Jordan)
- Week 1: Private PoC deployment in FastRetail VPC (Redwood Private control plane). Network & KMS setup. (Owners: Jordan + FastRetail infra)
- Week 2: Integrate Node.js SDK + REST fallback; ingest a sample dataset and run evals. (Owner: Marissa)
- Week 3: Load testing, latency/cost tuning, and shared dashboard. Finalize quality metrics. (Owners: Marissa + FastRetail eng)
- Week 4: Wrap-up, executive summary, and next-step recommendation for Dedicated vs Hosted.

Integration details we discussed:
- SDKs: Node.js as primary integration (official Redwood SDK). Python SDK for analytics jobs.
- API compatibility: REST endpoints + streaming responses supported; function-call style structured responses available for product–attribute generation.
- Auth: Customer-managed KMS for encryption; tokens scoped to PoC environment.

Attachments: I’ve attached a short PoC plan and an integration checklist (redwood-poc-plan.pdf, integration-checklist.xlsx).

Immediate next steps:
1) Elena: confirm PoC approval and share point-of-contact for infra (VPC CIDR and KMS contact).
2) Tom: share a 10–15 item eval set and a sample product feed we can ingest for Week 2.
3) Jordan/Marissa: we’ll send a calendar invite for a 30-min kickoff next Tuesday and provide access instructions for the Private control plane.

Thanks — happy to adjust if I missed anything.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jordan_blake@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Discovery recap & integration/onboarding plan - FastRetail PoC

Thanks Jordan — this summary looks great and captures the key points. A few quick notes: 

- We can approve the PoC scope; procurement will sign the PoC MSA by Wednesday EOD.
- Infra POC contact: Priya Singh (priya.s@fastretail.co) — she’ll share VPC CIDR and KMS owner details.
- I attached the 10–15 item eval set to this reply (see inline below). Tom will send the product feed by tomorrow.

Can we move the kickoff to Wednesday at 10am PT instead of Tuesday? That gives our infra team time to accept the MSA.

Elena
VP, Product Ops | FastRetail
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Discovery recap & integration/onboarding plan - FastRetail PoC

Perfect — thanks for the quick turnaround. Wednesday 10am PT works for us; I’ll send the invite.

Follow-ups / notes for the team:
- Marissa: please prepare the Node.js SDK quickstart and a short demo script that ingests the eval set and runs the embedding/retrieval evaluation.
- Logan: looping you in for visibility on the PoC MSA and any pricing/discount guardrails we should be aware of. If procurement pushes on contract terms, I may need a quick greenlight for a standard PoC concession.

Elena — to make onboarding frictionless, we’ll send a small step-by-step doc in advance with: control-plane access instructions, IP allowlist, and a sample env for KMS token setup.

Thanks — calendar invite sent.

Best,
Jordan
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Thanks — I’ve started a checklist for the Node.js quickstart and will attach a short demo script in the shared drive before the kickoff.

Quick clarifications I’ll cover in the demo:
- SDK methods for batch embedding ingestion and how to stream responses for generation.
- Fallback to REST API if you prefer a language-agnostic path.
- How we handle prefix/KV caching for product-description workflows to hit the latency targets.

I’ll also include the small synthetic load test script we use to validate throughput and the dashboard link so FastRetail can watch real-time metrics.
